intro_html: This is the walking taco in casserole form: seasoned beef and kidney bean chili baked under melted cheese, with salty corn chips for crunch. Each serving packs 37 grams of protein at about $2.62 a bowl. It tastes like the fair, minus the fair prices.
cost_closing_html: About $2.62 a bowl for what a stadium sells in a torn-open chip bag for $9. The chili itself is barely a dollar a serving; the chips are a quarter of the bill, so shop that chip sale hard.
shop_smart: The Fritos are $9.27 of this batch, about a quarter of the whole bill. Store brand corn chips knock a few dollars off, and under a ladle of chili nobody can tell.
Kidney beans do the heavy lifting: nearly 8 cans of cheap protein and fiber stretch 2.25 lb of beef into 14 big servings.
Buy the 3 lb pack of 93/7 beef and freeze the extra 0.75 lb for the next batch. The bigger pack beats the small tray on price per pound every time.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a big pot and cook the diced onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and break it up as it browns. Cook until no pink remains, then stir in the taco seasoning and salt.
Add the drained kidney beans, the diced tomatoes with green chilies with their juice, and the tomato sauce. Simmer 10 minutes so it thickens into a proper chili.
Spread the chili into a baking dish, top with the Mexican cheese blend, and bake at 350F until the cheese is melted and bubbly, about 15 minutes.
Portion the chili into 14 containers. Keep the corn chips in the bag; add a handful on top after reheating so they stay crunchy instead of turning to mush.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot of chili, subtract the empty pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is one serving in grams, plus its share of the chips at serving time. Each bowl comes out to about 686 calories and 37 grams of protein.
